title: Codify customer-facing degradation contracts and acceptance tests
creator: Priya Singh
description:
Background: Recent incidents (KV cache regen stalls and regional saturation) highlighted gaps in what customers see and what the runtime actually guarantees during degraded modes. Postmortem action items called for explicit, testable degradation contracts that are surfaced to customers and enforced with rollout/rollback gates.

Objective: Produce a PRD update and acceptance test suite that codifies customer-facing degradation contracts for common failure classes (model-variant fallback, latency tail, feature disablement), specifies console/SDK visibility, and defines automated verification (synthetic tests + CI) to prevent regressions. This ticket covers scoping, acceptance criteria, implementation checklist, and handoff to engineering for execution.
acceptance_criteria: Define a 3-tier degradation taxonomy (Tier 0: nominal, Tier 1: soft degradation - increased latency/cost, Tier 2: hard degradation - partial feature disablement or reduced model fidelity) with clear customer-visible messaging for each tier.

For each degradation tier, enumerate exact runtime behaviors: allowed latency percentile increases, permitted token-cost uplifts, allowed model-variant substitutions, and fallback order. All numbers must be defensible and accompanied by a rationale.

Console/UI: Add a per-route degradation contract panel that shows current tier, last triggered timestamp, and active fallbacks. Mockups and API spec must be attached to the PRD and reviewed by Design.

Automated verification: Implement three synthetic CI scenarios that reliably exercise each degradation tier and assert telemetry signals (SLO breach events, fallback invocation logs, and alert firing). Tests must run in staging on every runtime release pipeline.

Runbook + rollback: Provide step-by-step runbook excerpt for on-call including explicit rollback criteria tied to Tier 2 triggers and a post-rollback verification checklist. Runbook must reference existing incident page templates.
Customer communication: Draft standardized customer-facing phrasing for status pages and billing implications when Tier 1 or Tier 2 is entered. Legal/Support review must be completed.
Backward compatibility: Existing SDKs must continue to work; any console/API schema changes must be additive and documented in the release notes.

Metrics: Add three new dashboard panels in Grafana/Console showing (a) per-route tier history, (b) fallback counts by model variant, and (c) synthetic test pass rate. Dashboards must be linked in the PRD.
Acceptance sign-off: Product, Eng leads, Design, and Support must sign off on the PRD and test matrix before work is scheduled into a release.
Security: If any customer-visible artifacts include data samples, a security review is required (false by default for this ticket unless examples are added).

decision_log: 2026-02-18: Chosen approach: explicit customer-facing tiers rather than opaque 'degraded' flag to reduce support noise and enable predictable customer expectations.

2026-02-20: Trade-off: Tier 1 allows limited latency increases up to p99+50% for identified routes to preserve availability; this accepts higher per-token cost during soft degradation but avoids full feature loss.
2026-02-24: Decided to prioritize synthetic verification in CI over manual QA checks for early detection of regression; will run small nightly jobs in staging to keep cost low.

2026-03-01: Agreed fallback order: model-variant (same architecture quantized) -> lower-context-length variant -> degrade to 'concise' generation mode -> partial feature disablement. Documented reasons for ordering in PRD.
2026-03-03: Opted for additive Console API changes only; no breaking changes to SDKs. Any new fields will default to 'unknown' for older clients.
2026-03-04: Decision to require Support and Legal sign-off for all customer billing language tied to degradation tiers.
